outline_section.section_title: Checking Boundedness from a Signal Graph
outline_section.learning_goal: Classify boundedness directly from a graph by extracting extrema and verifying no unbounded divergence over time.

question_policy.answer_format: Classify each candidate graph as bounded or unbounded and select the matching bound description

distractor_plan: Mistake local extrema for global boundedness
Classify periodic-like centerline segments as unbounded
Use short-time endpoint behavior instead of all-time behavior

paragraph_plan: Use the same stepwise procedure as symbolic cases: read graph shape, test long-time trend, compute bounded envelope if any.
display_math_plan: \n|x(t)| \le M \text{ checks values for all } t\text{, including large positive/negative } t.\n

example_outline.worked_example_prompt: Use the displayed graph to decide whether x(t) is bounded. Explain by referencing long-run growth behavior and envelope candidates.
example_outline.worked_solution_goal: Demonstrate a clean boundedness decision from visual features without introducing unnecessary coordinate computation.
example_outline.variation_from_previous: Transfers from formula-based bounds to visual recognition with unchanged decision rule.
solution_step_plan: Identify whether amplitude remains within finite vertical limits for all t.
Check whether oscillations grow or drift without bound as t increases/decreases.
State bounded/unbounded and justify with the relevant visual evidence.

prompt_blocks.text: Use the graph below to classify $x(t)$. Which statement is correct?

choice_blocks.text: Bounded, with a valid finite bound such as $M=2$ (all values lie between two fixed envelopes).
Unbounded, because the local maxima increase from left to right in the displayed window.
Bounded in the shown window, but not enough to decide global boundedness unless negative and positive time tails are tested.
Unbounded, because the signal is periodic-like and periodic graphs always diverge.
Bounded with $M=\infty$ because the graph repeats regularly.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: A single finite envelope is visible for all shown time, and the graph stays between fixed levels. That matches the definition: there exists a finite $M$ with $|x(t)|\le M$ for all $t$ shown, and in this controlled graph family that envelope is global.

images.image_description: A continuous-time signal graph for x(t) over t from -5 to 5. Add small arrows on both sides of the plot indicating this envelope growth continues for larger |t| beyond the shown window. Axes labeled time and amplitude.

prompt_blocks.text: Use the graph below to classify $x(t)$ and identify the correct bound statement.

choice_blocks.text: Unbounded, because envelope magnitude grows as $|t|$ increases and no finite ceiling can hold all peaks.
Bounded, with $M=7$ from the shown interval.
Unbounded because the centerline looks like a periodic segment, which always implies divergence.
Bounded, because the right half is symmetric with the left half.
Classify as bounded on $[-5,5]$ and unbounded outside if endpoints continue with same trend, so classification is unresolved.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: This graph shows a growing envelope, so any fixed $M$ is eventually exceeded. Boundedness requires a finite envelope for all time; here growth in both directions violates that requirement.
